reasoning: Both are correct and secure. A wins because its Destroying handler keeps per-player state correct however a part is destroyed, and its comments explain why. B can count destroyed blocks toward the cap.

criteria.note: Creates both remotes and the PlacedBlocks folder, validates through PlacementRules.validate, builds the part from BlockTypes.STYLES, and enforces the cap and the os.clock cooldown; ownerOf/blocksOf/blockCount stay consistent through RemoveBlock, the Destroying handler, and PlayerRemoving.
RemoveBlock checks typeof, then IsA("BasePart"), then ownerOf[part] ~= player before destroying; PlaceBlock passes unknown values to PlacementRules before casting.
Comments explain why ownership is server-only and the attribute is never trusted, that Destroying covers other destroy paths, and why the tables are dropped before destroying.
Mostly terse inline comments; the ownership comment spans two lines but carries real content.
No change history and no references to the request.
Reuses BLOCK_SIZE, STYLES and validate, is strictly typed, and passes luau-lsp and selene; one StyLua line-wrap failure in the createBlock signature.
Meets all requirements, but blocks destroyed outside RemoveBlock stay in blocksByPlayer and keep counting toward the 150 cap.
onRemoveBlock destroys only a part found by table.find in the sender's own list, so foreign or arbitrary instances are rejected.
Its few comments are accurate ('-- seconds', the ownership note); the header description partly restates what the code does.
The ownership comment is two lines that could be one; section banners are at file level, not inside functions.
The @date header records history-like metadata, but there are no references to the request.
Reuses the shared modules, is typed, and passes luau-lsp and selene; one StyLua failure on the validate call.

strengths: The Destroying handler keeps counts right however a part is destroyed
Ownership lookup is O(1) and server-authoritative
weaknesses: warn on every rejected placement could spam the output

strengths: Removal is secure through a membership check in the sender's list
weaknesses: Does not handle blocks destroyed outside RemoveBlock, so dead entries can inflate the cap count
